report.source_text: Native T1-mapping demonstrated markedly elevated T1 values with preponderance in the inferoseptal wall (1068 ± 73 ms in the entire slice vs. 1122 ± 31 ms in the inferoseptal wall), also see Figs. 1a and 2a. Furthermore, T2-mapping revealed increased values (entire slice 52 ± 6 ms, inferoseptal wall 55 ± 6 ms), suggesting myocardial edema representing active myocardial inflammation by hantavirus infection. In contrast, the LGE image, potentially indicating irreversible myocardial damage if positive, in the corresponding slice was negative (Fig. 1c).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 36-year-old male presented with headache, abdominal pain, thrombocytopenia, elevated creatinine with proteinuria, elevated CRP, and positive Puumala virus IgG and IgM antibodies. Six days after admission, cardiac biomarkers were elevated (troponin I 0.32 μg/l, CK 319 U/l) without dynamic ECG changes. Cardiac MRI performed six days after admission showed markedly elevated native T1 and T2 mapping values indicating myocardial edema and active inflammation, with negative late gadolinium enhancement. Coronary CT angiography excluded coronary artery disease. Over the following weeks, the patient’s symptoms improved, supporting recovery from myocarditis.

CMR native T1 and T2 mapping showed increased values indicating myocardial edema and inflammation; LGE negative
coronary CT angiography ruled out coronary artery disease
clinical improvement with resolution of chest pain and dyspnea weeks after myocarditis diagnosis
